subject: QuickMart: conversation delivery delays and interim mitigations
messages:
From: Alyssa Turner <alyssa.turner@quickmart.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: platform@quickmart.com
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Live convo delivery delays since 09:05 PT

Hi Laura,

We started seeing slowed message delivery on our in-app support bot around 09:05 PT this morning. Instead of streaming tokens as they are generated, responses are arriving in 6–12s chunks (users notice a pause then a burst). It's impacting checkout flows — several customers have reported abandoned carts.

Example session ids (sampled): qmk-sess-22a7, qmk-sess-22b2.
We capture latency traces in the dashboard; I've attached two screenshots from our observer and a short session export.

Can Redwood advise temporary mitigations we can apply while you investigate? Short-term rollbacks, alternate endpoints, or configuration flags would be great.

Thanks,
Alyssa Turner
Head of Product Ops | QuickMart
Attachments: ticket-4721-screenshots.zip, session_debug_0904.txt
From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
To: Alyssa Turner <alyssa.turner@quickmart.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 09:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Live convo delivery delays since 09:05 PT

Hi Alyssa — thanks for the examples and the quick heads-up. We're seeing a correlated uptick in token emission tail times for your tenant in our US-west shard; investigating now.

Immediate steps we're recommending you try (safe, reversible):
- Switch the client from streaming to short polling (poll /responses every 250ms) for highest reliability while we triage.
- Reduce max_tokens per turn to 256 for the next 2 hours to limit long-tail generation bursts.
- If feasible, enable session-level prefix caching (client flag: x-rwd-prefetch: true) — this will reduce repeated KV lookups for your common prompts.

I'll escalate to our infra team and loop back with a targeted mitigation ETA in 30–45m. We will also share a post-incident timeline and credit offer after resolution.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference

Subject: URGENT: QuickMart elevated stream tail latency — assign owners

Team — QuickMart (QMK) reports streaming responses arriving as large bursts (6–12s). Impact: checkout disruption / revenue risk. Details from customer included.

Telemetry snapshot (preliminary):
- Increased 95/99 token-emit times for tenant across us-west edge cluster.
- Elevated queued-batch sizes on shard gw-14 / gpua-3.

Please own the following:
- Ben: triage kernel/runtime — look for batching window regression, overloaded KV cache, or degraded shard routing. Priority P0. Provide rollback options for any recent batching heuristic changes.
- Marissa: lead customer comms; share the short polling + token cap guidance and confirm when QuickMart applies. Track impact.
- Vivek: coordinate with infra on a temporary routing rule to avoid gw-14 if needed; prepare fallback model variant that favors latency (rwd-medium-fast).

I've attached the customer's screenshots and session dumps. I'll update after infra confirms mitigation.

Thanks,
Laura
Attachments: session_debug_0904.txt, incident_timeline_qmk-0904.csv
From: ben.carter@redwood.ai
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: URGENT: QuickMart elevated stream tail latency — assign owners

Quick triage notes:
- Root cause hypothesis: an aggressive batching-smoothing change pushed yesterday increased the batch-grace window for short sequences. Under normal load this improved throughput, but for high concurrency short-turn workloads (like QuickMart) it increased token tail times.
- Also saw a hot spot on gw-14 where a small percentage of sessions had elevated KV lookup times due to cache fragmentation.

Mitigations applied (10:00–10:03 PT):
1) Reverted batching-smoothing flag to previous value for us-west (~immediate effect).
2) Applied an expedited routing policy to divert new QuickMart sessions away from gw-14.
3) Enabled a temporary low-latency model fallback (rwd-medium-fast) for your tenant — slightly higher per-token cost but reduces tail times.

Preliminary impact: 50% drop in 95th-percentile token tail within 5 minutes after revert and routing change. Continue to monitor.

Next steps: full postmortem to follow with timeline and permanent config adjustments (longer-term: adaptive batching conditioned on short-seq fast-path).

— Ben
Ben Carter
SRE, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
To: Alyssa Turner <alyssa.turner@quickmart.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 11:10:00 -0700
Subject: Actions we took and recommended next steps — QuickMart incident

Hi Alyssa — update and concrete next steps for QuickMart.

What we saw: streaming token emission tails for sessions on us-west; correlated with a recent batching-smoothing change and a KV cache fragmentation event on a single gateway shard. This produced observable pauses followed by token bursts.

What we did (summary):
- Reverted the batching-smoothing change for us-west (immediate).
- Diverted QuickMart traffic away from the affected shard (gw-14).
- Enabled rwd-medium-fast fallback for your tenant (temporary — will revert after stabilization).
- Suggested client-side mitigations for you (short polling, reduce max_tokens, enable prefix caching).

Customer-facing mitigations for your app (please apply as you can):
1) Toggle to short polling for 60–120 minutes. Code example: poll /v1/responses?session_id=... every 250ms until you see steady streaming again.
2) Set max_tokens=256 for the next 2 hours.
3) If you can enable the x-rwd-prefetch flag, we will see fewer repeated KV lookups per turn.

We will:
- Continue monitoring and keep you updated every 2 hours until fully resolved.
- Run a post-incident review and share a write-up and timeline (we plan to deliver this within 72 hours).
- Issue a one-time usage credit to offset any customer impact; details in the postmortem.

Attachments: incident_timeline_qmk-0904.csv (timeline), session_debug_0904.txt (debug capture).

Can we schedule a 30-minute postmortem call Friday 09/04? Marissa will coordinate.

Best regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
